description: We are Polaris_101 , will be working on  the Field Shift challenge by developing a web app that leverages NASA weather history, soil metrics, and crop requirements to optimize seasonal farming decisions
summary: Field Shift is a data-driven decision-support platform designed to help farmers adapt to changing environmental conditions and improve agricultural sustainability. We developed a web-based solution that combines NASA Earth observation data, including soil moisture, land surface temperature, precipitation, and vegetation indices, with local soil information and farmers' priorities. The platform transforms these datasets into practical insights, helping users assess field conditions, identify potential agricultural risks, and make more informed decisions about crop selection, irrigation, and crop rotation. By making satellite-based information more accessible and understandable, Field Shift addresses the challenge of using Earth observation data to support real-world agricultural decisions. Our goal is to bridge the gap between complex environmental data and farmers' everyday needs, contributing to more resilient, efficient, and sustainable agriculture.
details:
What does Field Shift do?

Field Shift is an agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers and agricultural professionals understand environmental conditions and explore crop-rotation possibilities. It connects Earth observation data and agricultural information to provide a clearer picture of the factors influencing planting decisions.

How does it work?

The platform uses environmental and satellite-derived information to help users explore field conditions. It brings together relevant indicators, such as rainfall, temperature, vegetation conditions, and soil moisture where available, with crop characteristics and agricultural context.

Users can explore different crop-rotation scenarios and compare their characteristics and potential trade-offs. The objective is to make environmental information easier to understand and support more informed agricultural planning.

Who benefits from it?

Our primary target users are farmers, particularly those in regions exposed to climate variability and water scarcity. Agronomists, agricultural consultants, cooperatives, and researchers are also potential users.

Expected benefits and goals

Field Shift aims to:

  • Make Earth observation data more accessible and understandable.
  • Help users explore crop-rotation alternatives.
  • Support climate-aware agricultural planning.
  • Encourage more informed decisions about crop sequences and environmental conditions.
  • Demonstrate how space-based data can contribute to agricultural decision-making.

Tools and Technologies

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS for the interactive dashboard and farm-management interface.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI for NASA data requests, farm analysis, and AI-advisor endpoints.
  • Database and storage: SQLite for the backend crop catalog; browser local storage for farmer profiles, farms, and settings.
  • NASA and Earth observation data: NASA POWER for climate and weather indicators; Google Earth Engine for optional SMAP soil moisture, MODIS vegetation index, and SRTM terrain data.
  • AI integration: Groq through an OpenAI-compatible API, with the API key kept on the backend.
  • Maps and visualization: Leaflet and OpenStreetMap for farm maps; Recharts for charts; custom React components for risk calendars, crop history, and 3D farm simulations.
  • Deployment: Cloudflare Pages for the static frontend and Render for the FastAPI backend.
